citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (users cannot check which model answered)
citations.excerpt: A user querying a model today cannot check that the responses came from the specific model that a developer claims is responding, as opposed to one secretly substituted in by a routing service for cost reasons, or even by an attacker who has tampered with the token stream.

citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (routing-service clients want assurance)
citations.excerpt: Clients who use a model through a third-party routing service want assurance that the tokens came from the model they paid for.

citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (FlashProve throughput and proof size on Llama 4 Maverick)
citations.excerpt: For a large model (Llama 4 Maverick, 400B-parameter mixture of experts), a single H100 GPU generates proofs at around 110 tokens/second, with a proof size of ~19 MB per 1,024-token request, when in 4-bit quantized weights, using integer arithmetic in prefill.

citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (prover cost relative to vLLM)
citations.excerpt: This is ~70-95x the GPU time of running the model itself on vLLM, a common open-source library.

citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (limitation: integer model under greedy decoding)
citations.excerpt: The proof is about an integer model under greedy decoding.

citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (limitation: floating-point or sampled replies can depart)
citations.excerpt: A reply from a floating-point implementation, or sampled decoding, could depart at some position and no longer exactly match the computation proved.

citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (limitation: integer-to-float error excludes adversarial prompts)
citations.excerpt: The integer version is generally expected and empirically tested to be within some small error rate of true floating-point inference generically (even taking into account non-determinism of floating-point computations), though this does not cover adversarially designed prompts.

citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (limitation: 1,024-token contexts)
citations.excerpt: The system currently proves inference over contexts of up to 1,024 tokens.

citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (trusted hardware and cryptography are complementary)
citations.excerpt: Trusted hardware and cryptography are complementary approaches with different guarantees and tradeoffs.

citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (the production prototype signs traffic and recomputes on a trusted server)
citations.excerpt: we met that goal through a separate but related project, which signs our inference traffic and recomputes inference on a trusted server

citations.label: Cai, Shi, Zhao and Song (UC Berkeley), Are You Getting What You Pay For? Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs (arXiv 2504.04715) (providers may substitute quantized or smaller models)
citations.excerpt: Providers may covertly substitute cheaper alternatives (e.g., quantized versions, smaller models) to reduce costs while maintaining advertised pricing.

citations.label: Cai, Shi, Zhao and Song (UC Berkeley), Are You Getting What You Pay For? Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs (arXiv 2504.04715) (output-based and logprob detection are unreliable)
citations.excerpt: Our empirical analysis reveals that software-only methods are fundamentally unreliable: statistical tests on text outputs are query-intensive and fail against subtle substitutions, while methods using log probabilities are defeated by inherent inference nondeterminism in production environments.

citations.label: Cai, Shi, Zhao and Song (UC Berkeley), Are You Getting What You Pay For? Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs (arXiv 2504.04715) (TEEs give integrity guarantees at modest overhead)
citations.excerpt: Our findings demonstrate that TEEs can provide provable cryptographic guarantees of model integrity with only a modest performance overhead

citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (output alone is unreliable)
citations.excerpt: Judging from the model’s output alone is unreliable, even if it produces high-quality responses.

citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (a zkSNARK appended along with each response)
citations.excerpt: The provider can append, along with each response, a zkSNARK proving that the output was produced by the claimed model on the given input.

citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (post-hoc proving for a subset of tokens)
citations.excerpt: post-hoc proving (i.e. proving after-the-fact, for a subset of tokens). Our system follows the latter.

citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (post-hoc limitations: delay and non-determinism)
citations.excerpt: On the other hand, post-hoc proving has limitations: added complexity of recomputation, the delay in getting guarantees about your traffic, and inherent “non-determinism”.

citations.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team with EPFL, StarkWare, MIT and Succinct co-authors, Progress on provable inference for large language models (TEEs rely on the manufacturer's tamper-resistant hardware)
citations.excerpt: Prior work often focuses on  trusted execution environments  to achieve PI. These are hardware-based solutions that provide privacy and attestation that rely on the manufacturer producing tamper-resistant hardware.
